The visible anatomy matches the requested AP radiograph of a lower leg one view filling the frame with no pelvis or groin and the declared age and anatomical exceptions.

defects: Unexplained additional image findings: ["Extensive diffuse soft tissue calcifications in a stippled/popcorn pattern throughout the lower leg — not consistent with gas gangrene, which requires dark gas lucencies, not calcific densities"]

findings: Anteroposterior (AP) projection of the lower leg (tibia and fibula) with partial visualization of the knee joint superiorly and ankle mortise inferiorly

Extensive, diffuse, coarse heterotopic calcifications distributed throughout the soft tissues of the lower leg, appearing as multiple rounded and lobular radiodense foci in a stippled/popcorn-like pattern involving the muscle compartments
The soft tissue calcifications are bilateral in distribution within the leg and are extensive, spanning from the proximal to distal lower leg
Tibial and fibular cortices appear intact without discrete fracture line identified on this view
Bone density appears relatively preserved; no obvious aggressive periosteal reaction or cortical destruction identified
The calcifications are predominantly in the soft tissues rather than within the bone cortex or medullary canal
Knee joint space appears partially visualized at the superior margin; no obvious large joint effusion identified on this view
differential: Tumoral calcinosis (idiopathic or secondary, e.g., renal osteodystrophy/hyperphosphatemia) – extensive periarticular and soft tissue calcium deposits in a lobular/nodular pattern

Myositis ossificans progressiva (Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva) – progressive heterotopic ossification in soft tissues; however, classic FOP tends to show more sheet-like ossification rather than purely nodular calcification

Soft tissue chondromatosis or synovial chondromatosis with extraarticular extension / calcified soft tissue neoplasm (e.g., chondrosarcoma of soft tissue) – multiple calcified masses; less likely given diffuse bilateral distribution but included given extent of calcification
anatomyConcerns: Only a single projection (AP) is visible; a lateral view would be essential for complete characterization of the soft tissue calcifications and to assess for cortical abnormality
The proximal tibia and fibular head are partially cut off superiorly, limiting full assessment of the knee joint and proximal bone
The ankle and distal bones are partially included but incompletely imaged, limiting distal assessment
